programmes.d: Arsenic poisoning is found to be the cause of a woman's mysterious illness.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide. Investigators say it was murder — that it was physically impossible for the woman to have shot herself.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity. To solve the case, investigators turn to bug larvae found on the body and a tiny wad of chewing gum found near the victim's body.
This episode documents a deadly bombing at a church in Oakwood, Illinois, in December 1997.
While skeet shooting on a beautiful spring day, Martin Dillon is shot dead. His friend maintains it was a freak accident, but it takes more than 20 years for the truth to surface.
On Halloween night 2004, Adriane Insogna and Leslie Mazzara were brutally murdered in their Napa, California home.
Twenty years after the murder of a young mother technology sheds a new light.
The murder of an eccentric millionaire was more than just a robbery.

A young man was killed in a mysterious car crash, but the evidence at the scene led investigators to believe it was not an accident. Forensic science revealed what really happened and the truth devastated three families.
A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home.

A 19-year-old woman was found dead in her car; the scene had been staged to make murder appear to be suicide. During their investigation, police discovered the victim was involved in a love quadrangle, giving several people a motive to kill her.
When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity.
Professional photographer Charles Rathbun claims model Linda Sobek died during a consensual sexual encounter gone wrong, but Sobek's corpse and digital imaging tell a more sinister story.
17-month-old Josh Hinson died in a fire which a federal agency ruled was set by Josh's mother.
The victim had been stabbed more than thirty times and the crime scene was awash with her blood. Near her head, police discovered a distinctive button with strands of thread still attached.
In 1986, scientists and detectives use DNA to solve a string of rapes and murders in the UK.
A 34-year-old nurse experiences a variety of flu-like symptoms. None of her doctors are able to discover the cause, until she visits her gynecologist for a routine check-up.
To solve a triple homicide case, police had to delve into the world of high rollers.
Doctors don't know why a young scientist has fallen gravely ill. When tests finally reveal the cause, it's too late to save him.
In 1992, 22-year-old Dawn Bruce is brutally murdered in her Virginia apartment.

In 2007, Brian and Beverly Mauck were found dead in their Graham, Washington home. Using a bloody palm print and shoe prints at the scene, investigators focus their attention on Daniel Tavares, who had previously inked a tattoo on Brian's back.
A flu-like epidemic spreads throughout a Navajo reservation in 1983.
In 1996, 54-year-old Gayle Isleib was ambushed in her Manchester, Connecticut driveway and shot to death. Police had to determine whether obsessive love was the motive for her murder.
Police investigate a discarded sleeping bag containing bloody sneakers and a purse.
In this episode, the decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.
A search in Virginia's DNA databank reveals the identity of a news producer's murderer.

On September 17, 1984, in a suburb of Tucson, Arizona, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home on her pink bicycle to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned, but her slightly damaged bicycle was found nearby.
A flawed envelope is an unlikely clue to identifying a killer who laced a water cooler with cyanide.

Investigators sift through the ashes of a fire which killed a 40-year-old woman. The fire appears to have been started by an unattended cigarette. On closer look, forensic scientists discover the cause was far more complicated.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
By using techniques she saw on forensic science TV shows, a mother determines who was responsible for the accident that permanently injured her 4-year-old daughter.
The body of 16-year-old Leanne Tiernan was discovered nine months after she disappeared.
On a windy Kansas night in 1995, a mysterious fire swept through the home of a prominent doctor. In the debris, investigators found evidence which told them how the fire started.
Investigators look into the death of a teacher and discover that his death was not an accident.
In 1986, Gary Dale Larson was stabbed to death in his Edmond, Oklahoma home. The killer then sexually assaulted Larson's girlfriend, Janet Haynes.
The killer hoped to cover his tracks by staging the crime scene. But police saw through the attempt.

When an 11-year-old girl disappears from a remote Alaska town, investigators wonder if she has been attacked by a bear or become lost in the dense woods. Eventually, they realize that neither assumption is true.
A millionaire and his family were executed in their own home.

Police discover a bullet-riddled car, a missing driver and no witnesses. Had the victim been abducted or was she dead? The answers are found in a unique clue, so tiny it was measured in millionths of a meter.
A healthy man dies mysteriously in his sleep and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine.
When a man is gunned down in his own garage, investigators use science to unravel a twisted tale of lust, greed and deception.
When a woman exhibits flu-like symptoms before dying, investigators determine she was poisoned.

A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial. An expert witness has a different opinion as to how the fire started and, if proven, would clear the woman of any culpability.
Distinctive boots and a sweet tooth leads investigators to the killer of a WWII veteran.

In 1991, Maine resident Pearl Smith goes missing after an argument with her husband, Bill Bruns. When investigators find a blood trail that leads to the couple's basement, police are sure they'll find the victim's body.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a boy scout camp near Farmington, Missouri.
Investigators find a shoe print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints at a murder scene. But they believe the most telling piece of evidence is the bite mark on the victim's chest.
Seattle police had no suspects in the murder of a post-grunge singer for more than a decade.
Children die at an alarming rate at a Texas hospital, and one nurse may be involved.

One morning in a deserted area outside of Phoenix, a motorcyclist discovers the body of a young woman. She had been beaten, bound, strangled and possibly raped. Nearby plants tell investigators more about the killer.
A woman was killed instantly when a bomb exploded in her home. Who planted the bomb?

Shortly after daybreak, a fire is started in a dumpster in Vancouver. No one sees the arsonist or the fire, which burns for hours in the deserted parking lot. But there's more than garbage in this flaming container.
Foul play is suspected when Fort Worth factory worker Glenda Furch disappears after her shift.

They thought the fire would cover their crime. But one tiny clue, no bigger than a thumbtack, remained. It held all the information investigators needed to put a trio of cold-blooded killers behind bars.

In 1991, a high school girl vanished after attending a party. The prime suspect had two alibi witnesses for the night she disappeared. A solid alibi can often overcome circumstantial evidence, but forensic evidence is another matter.
The decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.
When anomalies stall a murder case, a candy wrapper and seeds help expose the killer.
After being admitted to the hospital with unexplained bleeding, 11-month-old Chad Shelton dies. Investigators and scientists frantically search for a cause when others from the same house fall ill.
A woman appears to have plunged her car into a creek. But investigators suspect foul play.
Flu-like symptoms of a mother and her children prove to be something more serious: thallium poisoning. After the mother's death, investigators turn their attention to finding the killer.
In 2007, Shamaia Smith disappeared from the strip club she worked at in East Hartford, CT.

Soon after organizing a workers' strike, a union official is executed in his home. Neither his wife nor anyone in the neighborhood hear any gunshots. It takes a forensic sound test, an electron microscope and a nightgown to explain why.
In a quiet village in Great Britain, a farmer came upon a chilling sight.
A Modesto, California teenager goes missing. With no signs of struggle in her home, police suspect she has simply run away — until her naked, bruised body is discovered in a ditch 20 miles away.
A husband and wife get shot, and their 16-year-old daughter manages to escape.
It's usually easy to determine how a criminal entered the crime scene. But in this case, it looked as if the killer vanished into thin air — and perhaps he had.
When Rosemary Anderson is found dead, her boyfriend confessed to her murder, but so did another man.

When the head chef of a historic Philadelphia restaurant was found dead, investigators interviewed the usual suspects: family, friends and coworkers. As they sifted through the evidence, police uncovered a chilling tale of debt and deceit.
In 2001, Ginger Hayes and her infant son Nicholas were abducted during a carjacking.

A woman is killed while walking her dogs in the woods. Since she has no enemies and her husband has an alibi, police assume it's a hunting accident — until they find a strange letter, allegedly written by the woman before her death.
In 1984, California firefighters battled ten arson fires in three weeks.

The body of a wealthy American businessman was found in his rental car. Teeth and bone fragments were the only remains. When the victim's wife files an insurance claim for $7 million, investigators seek the help of a renowned forensic anthropologist.
A killer is careless when a home is destroyed by fire and a young boy is missing.

In 2000, Christina Sanoubane was murdered in her Cedar Rapids apartment after moving away from her abusive boyfriend. There are clues at the scene: bloody footprints and DNA from the victim's rape kit.
A 19-year-old girl is found dead in her car in what appears to be a suicide.

A woman disappears without a trace. Even though foul play is suspected, the leads don't pan out and the trail turns cold. Twenty years would pass before police are able to link a clump of hair discovered in an isolated area with the missing woman.
A serial bomber was waging a vendetta against the legal profession.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
A man becomes the prime suspect when his parents are killed in a house fire.

When Scott Dunn goes missing, police spray his bedroom with Luminol and uncover a scene of horrific violence. Now investigators face a daunting task: proving that Scott Dunn had been murdered without a body, a witness or a murder weapon.
A routine missing persons report leads to a deadly love triangle and a murder charge.

It was one of the most brazen crimes of the 20th century. Adolph Coors III, chairman of the Coors Brewing Company, was kidnapped and held for ransom. The crime prompted one of the most intense manhunts in United States history.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.
In 1992, 22-year-old Dawn Bruce is brutally murdered in her Virginia apartment.

In the series premiere of "Forensic Files", the longest-running true crime series in history, a Connecticut flight attendant goes missing. Police suspect her husband is guilty of murder, but can they prove it?
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.

California police had several suspects in the robbery and brutal murder of an elderly couple. Ten years later, a determined forensic scientist used material from a dentist's office to uncover ballistic evidence that had been overlooked.
When a college co-ed vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal. If there was trace evidence, it had been washed away.
When a decomposed body is found stuffed in a barrel, it's easy to presume murder.

In 1971, John List left a note with the bodies of his mother, wife and three children in his mansion ballroom before disappearing completely. Detectives must solve the case, despite having only an outdated photograph of List.
A serial rapist is on the loose in a Texas town and no one knows where he'll strike next.
A young woman attends evening church services, then disappears. When her abandoned car is found, the tank is empty and a gas can she kept in her trunk for emergencies is missing.
Digital enhancement of security camera video shows that what appears to be a forced abduction.

The murder of an eccentric millionaire was not entirely unexpected; he flaunted his wealth and cared little for personal security. The evidence at the crime seemed to indicate robbery, but investigators wondered if there was something more.
Eyewitnesses description don't come close to resembling the prime suspect.

Two suspects are linked to a murder by bloodstained boots and a gun, but the owner of the items says he has never met the victim. Investigators hope manufacturing codes from beer bottles will determine who is telling the truth.
Alaskan hikers discover a body wrapped in sheets which were edged in orange stitching.
